title: TDDR Rising Narratives — Wednesday morning, Nov 18
summary: A snapshot of opposition narratives from the Right and the Far Left as of 7:20 AM ET Wednesday, Nov 18, 2026. Built for TDDR (Too Dumb Didn't Read). House Democrats vote behind closed doors this morning on their speaker nominee, and the Far Left's push against Hakeem Jeffries surged overnight. The Jeffries/AIPAC petition query jumped to 3,675 posts (3.68× its prior average), 3,513 of them since 5 PM ET, driven by a post claiming the petition to replace him passed 1.2 million signatures (15,334 views). Reports confirmed one million on Nov. 9; we could not verify 1.2 million, and Change.org signers are not verified voters. The ATM confrontation clip kept spreading (2,644 posts, 3.15×). Axios reports Jeffries has no challenger and members expect him to win easily. New on the Right: Turning Point Action's Tyler Bowyer claimed Arizona's new Democratic majority plans to repeal the state's ballot-harvesting ban ('They ran on affordability'). That query went from 3 posts in six days to 238 overnight. We found no 2027 bill; a 2026 repeal bill died in committee. Thune's 'third shutdown' warning is still climbing (460 posts, 3.45×). The Bovino-at-Rutgers story is fading fast (1,483 posts overnight, against 10,245 a night earlier) but still scores high against a quiet baseline. Disinformation: after Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there is 'zero evidence' the week's outages are linked or caused by hackers, an outage + cyberattack query still matched 27,760 posts in 24 hours, much of it calling the denials lies. It sits inside the FAA card and is not scored. Every count, quote, and fact-check comes from sources and X queries pulled this morning or carried over from last evening and labeled. Nothing here is invented.

None of the nineteen scored narratives appeared on the U.S. trends list, so no card received the trend bonus. We requested tweet_count, but the trend objects did not include it, so trend volumes are unavailable and we did not estimate them.

oppositionNote.body: Right = narratives the Right is pushing after the Democratic midterm wave. Far Left = pressure on Democratic leadership and the incoming majority from the party's left. Several stories this morning are worked by both sides. The Right shares the Jeffries ATM clip and the petition as a 'Democratic civil war,' and the shutdown card grows out of a real split among Democrats over using the Dec. 11 deadline to end the Iran war. The outage 'cyberattack' rumor is not clearly partisan, so it sits inside the FAA card rather than getting its own score. The tag is the primary opposition frame.

methodology: Last updated Wednesday, Nov 18, 2026, 7:20 AM ET. This is a research snapshot for TDDR, not a live API. U.S. X trends were pulled at about 7:11 AM ET. Last evening's snapshot (Nov 17, 5:40 PM ET) is kept in the archive and was not overwritten. Eighteen of its nineteen narratives were re-counted with the same queries so momentum compares like with like. The new 24-hour window overlaps last evening's by 10 hours (7 AM to 5 PM ET Tuesday), so we also report each query's 5 PM–7 AM ET overnight count against the same hours a night earlier. One narrative was dropped because it faded: Rep.-elect Don Leonard's 'red lines' for Jeffries (479 posts in the last 24 hours, 0.27× its prior daily average, down from 1,220 last evening); that thread is folded into the Jeffries/AIPAC card. One was added with a new query: the Arizona ballot-harvesting claim. Other candidates were counted and not carved out as cards: Dreamers/DACA 'amnesty' after Jeffries named the Dream and Promise Act a priority (378 posts, 0.17×; 303 overnight versus 43 a night earlier); Jeffries's Medicare/Citizens United agenda ahead of the vote (217 posts, 2.39×), which last evening's sample found was mostly supportive; Van Jones's comments on a Democratic messaging network (161 posts, 0.25×); and Rep. Tom Emmer's 'honeymoon' remarks, which X News summarized but our query matched only 2 posts. An outage + cyberattack/'coincidence' query (27,760 posts in 24 hours, 6.42×) is reported inside the FAA card and not scored; we rebuilt it this morning from last evening's description, so it may not match last evening's query exactly.

For each narrative we ran one English-language X search with x.get_posts_counts_recent at hourly granularity over a 167-hour window from 8:00 AM ET Wednesday, Nov 11 (the earliest whole-hour start the recent-count API allowed at pull time), through 7:00 AM ET Wednesday, Nov 18. The last 24 hourly buckets (7:00 AM ET Tuesday, Nov 17, through 7:00 AM ET Wednesday, Nov 18, exactly 24 hours) give the 24-hour count, and the whole window gives the 'seven-day' total. We counted named news or fact-check outlets whose coverage we opened or retrieved in this morning's searches and cite on the card. Official government pages, bill text, advocacy groups, research groups, pollsters, bill trackers, blogs, X News summaries, and X posts are cited as sources but not counted as outlets. We re-researched the Jeffries/AIPAC, Jeffries ATM, shutdown and FAA/outage cards plus the new Arizona card, and counted only outlets retrieved this morning on those cards, which is why some of their outlet counts changed. For the other cards, which we did not re-research this morning, the outlet count is carried over from last evening, and each of those cards says so. We noted whether each topic appeared on the U.S. trends list at about 7:11 AM ET.

Score = 50% volume index + 30% acceleration index + 20% coverage index. Volume index is 100 × log10(1 + last-24h posts) / log10(1 + the highest last-24h count in this set). Acceleration index is 100 × min(last-24h / prior daily average, 3) / 3, so a triple-or-higher average scores 100. Prior daily average is (seven-day total − last 24h) / 6. Coverage index is 70 × min(outlets, 7) / 7, plus 30 if the topic was on the U.S. X trends list this morning. The Arizona, shutdown, 'Make America Nice Again' and Bovino queries had low or spiky baselines, so their acceleration indices are maxed out on modest or falling volume; Bovino's 24-hour count includes Tuesday daytime, before it faded overnight. Read the post counts alongside the scores. Evening-to-morning score changes also reflect the lower volume ceiling (9,465 this morning versus 14,952 last evening) and how much coverage we retrieved.

Counts are query matches, not unique posts or unique users, and queries can overlap. The Jeffries/AIPAC, Jeffries ATM, Pressley and DSA queries share many speaker-race posts. The AOC query includes the bare word 'cast,' the shutdown query needs both 'shutdown' and an Iran/Medicaid/deadline term, and the rigged-midterms query also catches posts mocking fraud claims. Replies are included, and automated @grok replies make up a visible share of several queries, especially the outage query. Sentiment is a qualitative label from relevancy-sorted post samples and from quotes in news coverage, not a scientific poll. This morning we pulled fresh samples for the Jeffries/AIPAC, Jeffries ATM, shutdown, outage + cyberattack, USAID and Arizona queries. Other cards carry last evening's sentiment and say so. Daily bar charts use UTC days (a UTC day starts at 7:00 PM ET the previous evening). Bars marked * are partial windows. Hourly charts are labeled in ET.

disinfo.caveatBody: New this morning: there is still no evidence this week's outages are a cyberattack. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there is 'zero evidence' the incidents are linked or caused by hackers, criminals or a nation-state ('We are not under systemic attack'), and DNI Jay Clayton attributed them to patching and upgrades. Posts calling those denials lies drove an outage + cyberattack query to about 27,800 matches in 24 hours. PolitiFact found records do not support the claim that the Biden administration made the FAA system worse, and that Rep. Rosa DeLauro overstated the FAA's unspent communications money. 'Arizona Democrats are running a bill to legalize ballot harvesting' is unconfirmed: we found no 2027 bill, and the 2026 repeal bill that died in committee kept felonies for buying or tampering with ballots. 'Dems have been ballot harvesting in Arizona for eight years' comes with no evidence. On the left, the '1.2 million signatures' against Jeffries is unverified (reports confirmed one million on Nov. 9), and Change.org signers are not verified voters. Carried over: the Nov. 17 blackout hoax (PolitiFact: False) passed without a blackout; 'Democrats will defund the military to shut down the government' is misleading, since the push is about Iran-war funds; 'Gov. Sherrill tried to stop Bovino from speaking' is misleading; 'AOC is an actor who answered a casting call' twists a real, public recruitment; 'Texas Democrats banned guns for under-21s' is false (HB 606 is only prefiled); 'Jeffries took $1.5 million from AIPAC' conflates different money streams; Lead Stories found no '30,000-case' Texas voter fraud probe; the reparations bill (SB 376) does not pay reparations and is only prefiled; and 'Slotkin is a CIA asset' remains unsupported.

narratives.title: NEW: 'They ran on affordability, then came for the ballot-harvesting ban' — the Right pre-bunks Arizona's new Democratic majority

narratives.sentiment: Suspicious, pre-emptively alarmed ('so they can cheat')
narratives.sentimentNote: In a relevancy sample of posts from the last 24 hours, top matches were Tyler Bowyer's and Seth Keshel's posts and copies of them ('Ran on groceries. A few replies argued a repeal would backfire on Democrats or that voters, not legislators, should set election rules by initiative. This is a read of that sample, not a poll.
narratives.summary: New this morning. The query matched 238 posts in the last 24 hours, against 3 in the six days before, so its acceleration is capped; read the small volume alongside the score. Almost all of it came overnight: 236 posts from 5 PM to 7 AM ET, against 0 in the same hours a night earlier, peaking at 40 posts in the 8 PM ET hour Tuesday. It started with Turning Point Action's Tyler Bowyer, who posted at 2:45 PM ET Tuesday that 'Arizona's Deputy Secretary of State is now openly telling county elections officials that Democrats plan to run a bill to repeal the prohibtion on ballot harvesting. They ran on "affordability"' (1,386 likes, 465 reposts, 35,383 views). Seth Keshel followed with 'pretty clear Dems have been ballot harvesting in Arizona for the past 8 years' (848 likes, 235 reposts, 21,602 views) and a 'rumor mill' post that Bowyer reposted, and X News summarized it as 'Arizona Democrats Plan to Repeal Ballot Harvesting Ban After Election Win.' What we could confirm: Democrats flipped both chambers of the Arizona Legislature (at least 37 of 60 House seats and 20 of 30 Senate seats, per AP via Votebeat) and their session opens Jan. 11. Votebeat and the Arizona Mirror report their election agenda centers on restoring the Permanent Early Voting List and repealing or rewriting post-2020 Republican election laws. KJZZ reports Democrats are replacing the House elections committee with a Democracy, Civil Rights and Government committee. A Democratic bill to repeal the 2016 ballot-collection ban, HB 2511, was introduced in January 2026 and died in committee under the Republican majority; its text kept felonies for paying for ballots, tampering with them, posing as an election official, or failing to turn collected ballots in. We found no news report confirming the Deputy Secretary of State's reported comments, and no 2027 bill text. Arizona Mirror and Phoenix New Times reported in April that Turning Point itself collected ballots in Salt River Project board elections, which are exempt from the ban.
talkingPoints: They ran on affordability — then opened with your neighbor's ballot.
Decriminalizing ballot harvesting makes cheating easier.
Dems have been harvesting ballots in Arizona for years; now they want it legal.
Politicians don't own the election rules — voters do.
Chain of custody. Paper ballots. Same-day results.
narratives.amplifiers: @tylerbowyer (1,386 likes, 465 reposts, 35,383 views); @RealSKeshel (848 likes, 235 reposts, 21,602 views); @mattevans85; @PetitionerMeme; @Guszilla. X News carried a summary Tuesday evening.
narratives.whyItWorks: 'Ballot harvesting' is a pejorative the Right has spent a decade defining, and Arizona is where 2020 fraud claims ran deepest. Pairing it with 'they ran on affordability' turns the new majority's first election bill into proof of bad faith before any bill is filed, and it plants doubt about 2028 results in advance.
narratives.audience: Arizona conservatives, election-integrity activists and the Turning Point network, and a national MAGA audience primed by 2020 Arizona claims.
narratives.counter: Ask for the bill: none has been filed for 2027. Last session's version kept felonies for buying, selling or tampering with ballots. Family, household and caregiver exceptions already exist, and Turning Point collected ballots itself where the law allowed it. Then name the actual Democratic priorities, like restoring the early-voting list, in plain terms.

Votebeat and the Arizona Mirror list restoring the Permanent Early Voting List as the top Democratic election priority. Rubio wants you to believe…' (@EmilyandMe2, 7,904 views), lists of every outage since Nov. 10, and a post asking Grok 'which country is home to' a list of affected companies (1,504 likes, 651 reposts, 44,078 views), insinuating a foreign hand. On Tuesday, Apple said an internal update caused problems with iCloud, Apple Pay and the App Store (CBS News, Reuters); The Guardian reported Gmail problems, while Google said it saw no broad disruption; and the NSA said an outage of its internal network was 'scheduled routine maintenance' (CNBC). narratives.whyItWorks: A miserable travel weekend needs a villain, and the official explanation hands each side one: the Right gets a contractor, a decades-old system, and a funding ask, plus the 'Mayor Pete did it too' callback; Democrats get a resignation demand and an oversight hook.

narratives.counter: Use the FAA's own words: two sites, one contractor, about 60 routers patched, and a root cause still under investigation. 'No indication of a cyberattack' is the official position, and so is 'still investigating.' On Buttigieg: the 2024 Christmas Eve stop was one airline's vendor outage, not a failure of the national airspace system. Ask for a date for the final report.

factChecks.claim: The Biden administration made the FAA's system worse and caused the ground stop by wiring copper into fiber.
factChecks.detail: PolitiFact found available public records, audits and FAA investigations do not substantiate the claim; modernization delays span more than two decades and both parties. It also found Rep. Rosa DeLauro's claim that $12.5 billion 'largely remains unspent' overstated the communications money: $4.75 billion was earmarked for telecommunications modernization.

factChecks.claim: This week's Apple, Gmail, NSA, bank, Microsoft and FAA outages are a coordinated cyberattack.
factChecks.detail: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Nov. 17 there is 'zero evidence' the incidents are related or caused by hackers, criminals or a nation-state: 'We are not under systemic attack' (AP, BBC). DNI Jay Clayton said 'This is not a cyberattack, and this is not a coordinated effort by a nation-state' and attributed disruptions to patching and upgrades (ABC News). Apple cited an internal update and the NSA scheduled maintenance. These are official positions; we did not independently verify them, and no fact-check outlet has rated the combined claim.

factChecks.claim: A nationwide 90-day blackout will begin Nov. 17, 2026.
factChecks.detail: FEMA and the FCC are running a routine Emergency Alert System test at about 2:20 PM ET Nov. 17, required at least every three years, on TV and radio only. A TikTok video of Trump 'announcing' a blackout was manipulated from a Nov. 9 news conference. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said Americans do not need to stockpile.

factChecks.claim: Monday's outages at Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo and other banks were a cyberattack, part of the same attack as the FAA ground stop.
factChecks.detail: JPMorgan Chase said a software bug in on-premise hardware caused delays, that there is 'no evidence this is cyber-related,' and that other banks were affected only where they were party to Chase transactions (AP, CNBC). A Justice Department official told MS NOW there was 'no evidence of any attack' and no indication the disruptions are connected to Friday's outages. The FAA has said it has no indication Friday's ground stop was a cyberattack.

factChecks.claim: A cyberattack caused Friday's nationwide FAA ground stop.
factChecks.rating: False, per the FAA — root-cause investigation still open
factChecks.detail: The FAA's Sunday Q&A says 'Based on all available evidence, we have no indication that this was a cyberattack or an outside nefarious actor,' and traces the data flood to two sites, including one where L3Harris deployed a new router. The FAA and L3Harris 'continue to investigate the root cause,' and no final report has been published. This restates the official position; we did not independently verify it.

factChecks.claim: The FAA's new AI-assisted SMART system caused the ground stop.
factChecks.detail: The FAA's Sunday Q&A says 'The two systems are not related. SMART is a data aggregator, and it does not feed information into the air traffic control system.' We did not independently verify the vendor architecture; this rating restates the agency's denial.
